low golden sunlight rakes straight down the street, every hoof-kicked puff of dust lit like amber smoke, long shadows reaching from the boardwalk posts
high-noon sun hammers straight down, heat-haze shimmering the far end of the street into liquid silver, air thick and wavering above the baked dirt
a dust-devil spins lazily down the empty street, its pale column catching the afternoon glare, scattering grit across the sun-bleached boardwalks
thunderheads build green-black at the horizon, swallowing the sun and dropping the street into a bruised, yellowish half-light that turns every timber ominous
soft golden-hour light gilding the false fronts, long amber warmth soaking into the weathered wood, the street below pooling in gentle purple shadow
cool blue dusk settles over the street, lamplight beginning to glow amber in the saloon windows, the air gone still and faintly silver
pale morning mist clings low to the street, the early sun a white disk burning through it, boardwalks and hitching posts fading into gauze at fifty yards
wind drives a curtain of stinging grit down the street, a tumbleweed bounding past in the brown haze, the sun reduced to a pale copper smear
red-gold sunset floods the entire street end to end, every dust mote ignited, the false fronts blazing like hammered copper against a bruised violet sky
sudden summer rain sheets down, the street dissolving into dark mud puddles that mirror a jagged sky, every drop striking a tiny circle of reflected silver
dead-still midday heat presses the street flat, not a breath of air moving, white sun overhead bleaching the dust to bone, shadows pooled directly underfoot
a thin overcast softens the midday glare to a featureless pewter, no shadows anywhere, the street looking washed-out and pale as old chalk
first light of dawn slides cold and pink along the rooflines, the street below still held in gray shadow, a thin frost-haze rising from the damp ground
approaching wildfire smoke drifts in from the hills, turning the sun a deep blood-orange and filling the street with a dry, acrid amber murk
a fast-moving cold front shoves purple-gray clouds across the sun, light flickering between bright and dark every few seconds, dust swirling in unpredictable gusts
moonlight floods the empty street in cold blue-white, the dirt almost luminous, every hitching post throwing a sharp black shadow straight across the pale ground
a brief clearing after rain lets a single shaft of sunlight break through heavy cloud, spotlighting a stretch of wet mud that gleams like polished iron
thick afternoon haze from cook-fires and horses hangs in the still air, the westering sun diffused into a wide halo of dusty bronze light
the last sliver of sun drops below the ridgeline and the street goes into deep blue shadow instantly, the sky above still burning with trailing amber light
a dry electric stillness before a storm, air faintly greenish, light flattened and strange, dust lying oddly quiet as if holding its breath
blowing snow thin enough to see through swirls down the street, the pale winter sun barely visible, every plank of the boardwalk rimmed in white
a streak of sunlight breaks between two cloud banks and rakes the street at a shallow angle, turning the floating dust into a river of bright gold motes
heavy spring rain hammers the awning canvas and bounces off the street in a white mist of tiny splashes, the storefronts barely visible through the grey curtain
late autumn afternoon light comes in low and honey-warm, the air almost haze-free for once, every grain of street dirt casting its own tiny sharp shadow
a lull in the wind drops a sudden hush over the street, the dust settling slowly back to earth through slanted afternoon light, the air going glass-clear and still
